nodes.description: The central arm. Brain imaging shows global atrophy and autopsied brains are reduced in weight; functional imaging in one kindred suggested medial frontal and thalamic hypometabolism. As in the nerve, the pathology is axonal loss without infiltrative inclusions, so this is not a proteinopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in DNMT1 cause hereditary sensory neuropathy with dementia and hearing loss.
evidence.snippet: Brain imaging of affected persons showed global atrophy and reduced weight of autopsied brains.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in DNMT1 cause hereditary sensory neuropathy with dementia and hearing loss.
evidence.snippet: Pathologic studies of affected persons' nerve7, brain14 and spinal cord (Fig. 1) show axonal loss without interstitial infiltrative inclusions.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion. Causal variants cluster in the targeting sequence (TS, also RFTS) domain encoded by exons 20 and 21, and the residues involved sit in the hydrophobic core or the linker between the domain's two subdomains rather than at the catalytic site. Expressed in bacteria, wild-type TS domain is soluble while the mutant domains form inclusion bodies - direct evidence of misfolding rather than of an altered but folded protein.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in DNMT1 cause hereditary sensory neuropathy with dementia and hearing loss.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, the TS mutants form inclusion bodies, a strong indication that they are misfolded (Supplementary Fig. 2).

evidence.reference_title: Defects of mutant DNMT1 are linked to a spectrum of neurological disorders.
evidence.snippet: Five novel mutations of DNMT1 were discovered; p.C353F, p.T481P, p.P491L, p.Y524D and p.I531N, all within the target-sequence domain, and two mutations (p.T481P, p.P491L) arising de novo.

nodes.description: The epigenomic phenotype, and the reason this disease is not simply "loss of methylation". Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing of three patient-sibling pairs found consistent methylation loss across all chromosomes, with X and chromosome 18 most affected, and over half a million differentially methylated CpG sites. Hypomethylation predominates in promoters, exons, most CpG islands and repeat classes - but within some CpG islands hypermethylated sites outnumber hypomethylated ones, and imprinted genes carry more differentially methylated sites than non-imprinted genes. A maintenance enzyme that is mistargeted rather than simply absent produces exactly this mixed picture.

evidence.reference_title: Aberrant signature methylome by DNMT1 hot spot mutation in hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy 1E.
evidence.snippet: In the 3 affected siblings, overall methylation loss was consistently found in all chromosomes with X and 18 being most affected.

evidence.reference_title: Aberrant signature methylome by DNMT1 hot spot mutation in hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy 1E.
evidence.snippet: In some CpG islands, hypermethylated CpGs outnumbered hypomethylated CpGs. In 201 imprinted genes, there were more DMCs than in non-imprinted genes and most were hypomethylated.

evidence.reference_title: Aberrant signature methylome by DNMT1 hot spot mutation in hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy 1E.

nodes.description: The peripheral arm. Quantitative sensory testing, nerve conduction studies and nerve biopsy all indicate progressive sensory axonal loss in a length-dependent distribution, with nerve pathology showing axonal loss without inflammatory or infiltrative inclusions. Sensory nerve action potentials are absent while motor conduction is near-normal, which is what makes this a pure sensory neuropathy rather than a sensorimotor one.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in DNMT1 cause hereditary sensory neuropathy with dementia and hearing loss.
evidence.snippet: Quantitative sensory testing, nerve conductions, and nerve biopsy were indicative of length dependent progressive sensory axonal loss.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutation in the replication focus targeting sequence domain of DNMT1 causes hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy IE.
evidence.snippet: Electrophysiological studies revealed absent sensory nerve action potential with nearly normal motor nerve conduction studies.

nodes.description: The cellular consequence. DNMT1 is highly expressed in postmitotic neurons despite its canonical role being replication-coupled, which is the standing puzzle of this disease: how a maintenance methyltransferase defect damages cells that are not dividing. Cells expressing mutant DNMT1 are apoptosis-prone and fail to enter the neuronal lineage in differentiation assays.

evidence.reference_title: DNMT1 mutations found in HSANIE patients affect interaction with UHRF1 and neuronal differentiation.
evidence.snippet: Despite its well-known replication-coupled function as maintenance DNA methyltransferase in proliferating cells, DNMT1 is highly expressed in embryonic and adult postmitotic neurons, especially in the central nervous system (CNS)

nodes.description: Three consequences of the same misfold, which is why they are one node rather than three. The protein is degraded in late S and G2 phase; it fails to remain associated with heterochromatin when it should; and it loses the UHRF1 interaction that normally delivers it to hemimethylated substrate after replication. The enzyme's catalytic domain is intact, so this is a failure of delivery and persistence rather than of chemistry - which is why measured methyltransferase activity falls without the active site being touched.

evidence.reference_title: Aberrant signature methylome by DNMT1 hot spot mutation in hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy 1E.
evidence.snippet: The mutant DNMT1 protein shows premature degradation and reduced DNA methyltransferase activity.

nodes.description: There is no disease-modifying therapy. The intervention with the clearest mechanistic rationale is preventing the injury the patient cannot feel: daily foot inspection, protective socks and shoes, and avoiding exposures that would injure skin with reduced sensation. This targets the downstream complication - infection and amputation - rather than the neuropathy.
nodes.id: Protective Foot and Skin Care for the Insensate Limb

evidence.snippet: The emphasis of management is to help affected individuals and their caregivers understand the sudomotor defect and injury prevention when sensory impairment is significant.
Examination of feet daily for evidence of skin injury; annual routine clinical testing for dementia and audiogram to monitor hearing loss.

nodes.description:
Symptomatic, and directed at the neuropsychiatric end of the disease rather than at the neuropathy. GeneReviews names sedative or antipsychotic drugs for the restlessness, roaming, delusions and hallucinations that accompany the dementia. This is the treatment for two phenotypes this entry already curates - Dementia and Auditory or visual hallucinations - which previously had none.
No agent, dose or trial is named in the source, and none should be inferred here. The recommendation is a class-level statement of what helps, not evidence that a particular drug was studied in this disease.
nodes.id: Sedative or Antipsychotic Pharmacotherapy for the Behavioural Symptoms of Dementia

evidence.snippet: Sedative or antipsychotic drugs help to reduce extreme restlessness, roaming behavior, delusions, and hallucinations associated with dementia.
